findings.reason: both passages that define the live window's run must defer to the owner's key verbatim, or a future edit to `counter_run_continues` silently desyncs the panel from the store a third time.
findings.text: the `live` block decides "one run" as a contract distinct from the store's: it checks the job-id set and per-counter monotonicity (`_monotonic`, live_panel.py:243) but never the host or boot, while the owner `counter_run_continues` (telemetry_index.py:694) ends a run on any change to the key `(host, boot_id, job_id)`. The plan makes this worse rather than better: §11's design paragraph (plan.html:675) says "the same job, and no counter below its predecessor", and §12's read-back addendum (plan.html:729) restates `counter_run_continues` itself as "a run continues while its job is unchanged and no counter falls" — both of which drop the host and boot the named function actually keys. A serve that rolls to another host or reboots within the 45 s window therefore reads as one run in the live panel and as two in the index, which is exactly the drift §8 ("a run is defined twice … free to drift") was repaired to prevent.

findings.reason: the addition is a single derived percentage, it merges cleanly into the lane document's existing published fields, and it is already landed, so accounting for it changes no further node.
findings.text: the section introduces `lane.availability_percent` as a new public definition and publishes it top-level in `lane.json`, but its own text names neither a definition this retires or merges nor a reason nothing can be, against the one-rule requirement for any section adding surface.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §11's `live_panel.py` hides the lane-document digest and the receipt-tail differencing behind `lane_block` (live_panel.py:430), `live_block` (live_panel.py:347) and `live_panel` (live_panel.py:503), and §12's `provider_prices.py` hides fetch, age, atomic write and one-time migration behind one module; both are smaller interfaces than what they hide.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the live window's run boundary is implemented a second time in `live_panel.py` instead of importing its owner, `counter_run_continues` in `imas_ambix/agent/telemetry_index.py:694`.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §11 accounts for its added `--live` option and its two published blocks (it states why nothing retires — the readers it replaces live in the dotfiles repo — and why `--live` cannot merge into `--json`), but §14 lands `lane.availability_percent`, a new PUBLIC definition, without naming what it retires or merges or stating why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan cites the mechanism it extends at each proposal (counter_span, _prefix_hit_rate, ledger_cost/match_price/price_at, SiteConfig, lane.py, serving_receipts.tier_paths, telemetry_index.counter_run_continues, telemetry_retention.compare_tiers), and the outstanding sections name the index mechanism (§13) and the panel's own pct() helper (§15) they build on rather than proposing new machinery.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the only wrapper the plan adds is §9's single estimate-record reader in `watch.py`, which carries validation (`estimated_cost` refuses an unpriceable rate) and is justified in-text as the one reader gpu-watch will inherit through (`§9`: "never a constant repeated inside two tools"), so it is not a pass-through over machinery that could simply be extended.
